"An exemption of the exemption amount for the taxpayer; and an additional exemption of the exemption amount for the spouse of the taxpayer if a joint return is not made by the taxpayer and his spouse, and if the spouse, for the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins, has no gross income and is not the dependent of another taxpayer."

So for Alice to claim an exemption for Bob under section 151(b), the following conditions must be met:
1. A joint return is not made by Alice and Bob
2. Bob has no gross income for the calendar year 2015 (the calendar year in which the taxable year begins)
3. Bob is not the dependent of another taxpayer

**Facts analysis:**

- Bob has no income for 2015 (condition 2 is met)
- The claim states "Alice can receive an exemption for Bob under section 151(b) for the year 2015"

The key issue here is whether Alice CAN receive this exemption. The statute says the exemption is available if:
1. A joint return is NOT made by the taxpayer and spouse
2. The spouse has no gross income
3. The spouse is not the dependent of another taxpayer

The facts tell us:
- Bob has no income for 2015 ✓

But the facts don't explicitly tell us:
- Whether Alice and Bob filed a joint return
